scenes.title: Safe Arrival and Arctic Daydream
scenes.summary: Walton opens his letter from St. Petersburgh, reassuring his sister Margaret that his enterprise has begun without disaster. Braced by the cold northern breeze, he launches into a fervent, romantic vision of the pole not as desolation but as a region of eternal light, beauty, scientific discovery, and glory for mankind.

scenes.title: Origins, Hardship, and Doubt
scenes.summary: Calmed by steady purpose, Walton traces the origins of his obsession from childhood reading of voyages, through a failed year as a poet, to six years of deliberate hardening with whale-fishers. The recollection turns vulnerable as he confesses fluctuating hopes and depression and pleads for encouragement before his difficult voyage.

scenes.title: Plans for Archangel and Farewell
scenes.summary: Walton turns practical, describing pleasant sledge travel in Russia in furs and his plan to leave for Archangel to hire a ship and whaling crew for a June sailing. He admits he may be gone years or never return, then closes with a tender farewell blessing and his signature.

scenes.title: Frozen Waiting at Archangel
scenes.summary: Walton opens his letter from Archangel, restless in frost and snow but encouraged that his enterprise advances as he hires a vessel and engages dependable, courageous sailors.

scenes.title: The Want of a Sympathetic Friend
scenes.summary: Walton confesses his severe want of a cultivated, sympathetic friend to share his joys, sustain him in dejection, and regulate his ardent, self-educated mind, then finds no such companion on the ocean or in Archangel, praising only his courageous, glory-seeking English lieutenant.

scenes.title: The Generous but Uneducated Master
scenes.summary: Walton praises his gentle, brave, and upright master and recounts his noble sacrifice of his farm and prize-money to unite a young Russian lady with her poor lover, yet finds him wholly uneducated and silent and therefore insufficient as a friend.

scenes.title: Fixed Fate and Fond Farewell
scenes.summary: Resolve returns with trembling, half-pleasurable anticipation for unexplored regions and the marvellous, closing in tender affection as Walton affirms his fixed purpose while asking for his sister's letters and remembrance if he never returns.

scenes.title: Safe and Well Advanced
scenes.summary: Walton addresses his sister Margaret from high latitude on July 7th, reporting he is safe and well advanced. He notes his men remain bold despite drifting ice, dismisses gales and a leak as trifles, and promises to be cool, persevering, and prudent.

scenes.title: The Determined Heart
scenes.summary: Walton's tone swells into exultant ambition, declaring success will crown his efforts and nothing can stop a determined heart. He checks himself, blesses his beloved sister, and signs off.

scenes.title: Trapped in Ice and the Giant Apparition
scenes.summary: Walton opens his August 5th journal trapped by fog and closing ice. When the mist clears, the crew beholds vast plains of ice and a gigantic figure on a dog-drawn sledge racing north, filling them with anxious wonder before the ice breaks and frees the ship.

scenes.title: The Stranger on the Ice
scenes.summary: At dawn the crew finds a second sledge on drifting ice with one surviving dog and a frozen, emaciated European. He refuses rescue until Walton confirms the ship is bound for the North Pole, then collapses and is revived with brandy, blankets, and soup.

muse_override.reason: A frozen European rescued from ice sparks astonishment and mystery amid Arctic suspense and pity.

scenes.title: Recovery in Walton's Care
scenes.summary: After two days unable to speak, the stranger partly recovers and is moved to Walton's own cabin, where Walton nurses him and observes his shifting expression between wild despair and grateful benevolence.

scenes.title: To Shield the Stranger's Repose
scenes.summary: As the stranger slowly recovers, Walton shields him from the crew's idle curiosity. Pressed by the lieutenant about his strange ice journey, the stranger's face darkens: he came to seek one who fled from him in the same fashion. Told that such a sledge with dogs was seen the day before, he eagerly questions its route, calling the traveller a daemon, then thanks Walton alone for considerate forbearance.

scenes.title: To Watch for the Other Sledge
scenes.summary: The stranger gratefully acknowledges that Walton has benevolently restored him to life, then anxiously asks whether the breaking ice destroyed the other sledge. Walton cannot answer with certainty. Revived by hope, the stranger burns with a new spirit of life and eagerness to watch on deck for the sledge, but Walton persuades the still-weak man to remain in the cabin while others watch for him.

scenes.title: Unhappy Man Who Shares My Madness
scenes.summary: By August 13th Walton loves the gentle, noble stranger as a brother. When Walton confesses his burning ardour to sacrifice everything for polar discovery, gloom spreads over his listener, who weeps, groans, and cries out against sharing his madness and drinking the intoxicating draught, before grief overcomes him.

scenes.title: A Shared Longing for Perfect Friendship
scenes.summary: The stranger masters his despair and invites Walton's personal history. Walton confesses his thirst for intimate sympathy and a dearer friend, and the stranger agrees men are half-made without such aid to perfect them, mourns that he once had the noblest friend but has now lost everything, then withdraws in calm grief to his cabin.

scenes.title: A Rhapsody on Genius and Nature
scenes.summary: Alone, Walton rhapsodizes in his letter on the stranger's double existence, still elevated by starry sky and sea despite broken spirit, and praises his intuitive discernment, penetration into causes, facility of expression, and soul-subduing voice that raises him immeasurably above other men.

scenes.title: Promise of a Marvellous Tale
scenes.summary: On August 19th the stranger solemnly offers his history as a moral warning lest Walton's quest become a serpent to sting him. Walton burns with curiosity and sympathy, but the stranger insists his fate is irrevocably determined and promises to commence his marvellous tale the next day, which Walton vows to record.

scenes.title: An Honourable Father and a Fallen Friend
scenes.summary: Victor introduces his distinguished Genevese father and recounts how his father lost his proud merchant friend Beaufort to poverty and resolved to seek him out.

scenes.title: Misery in Lucerne and Rescue
scenes.summary: In a wretched street in Lucerne, Beaufort sinks into sickness and dies, while his daughter Caroline survives by humble labor until Victor's father arrives as a protecting spirit and takes her to Geneva.

scenes.title: A Marriage of Gratitude and Shelter
scenes.summary: Despite their age difference, Victor's father loves his mother with gratitude and reverence, sheltering her like a fair exotic and taking her on a tour of Italy to restore her health after her sorrows.

scenes.title: An Idolized Childhood in Naples
scenes.summary: Born at Naples and their only child for years, Victor accompanies his parents through Italy, Germany, and France, raised as their idol and plaything with tender caresses, patience, charity, and self-control.

scenes.title: The Cottage Child on Lake Como
scenes.summary: On the shores of Lake Como, Caroline visits a destitute cottage and is struck by a thin, fair-haired, blue-eyed girl among dark-eyed children. The peasant woman explains she is the orphaned daughter of a Milanese patriot devoted to Italian liberty and his deceased German wife, left a beggar after his property was confiscated.

scenes.title: The Promised Gift
scenes.summary: With Alphonse's permission Caroline prevails on the rustic guardians to yield Elizabeth Lavenza, who becomes the inmate of the Frankenstein house. Adored by all, she is presented to Victor as his promised gift, his more than sister and beloved companion.

scenes.title: Harmonious Childhood
scenes.summary: Victor recalls an idyllic, harmonious childhood in Geneva and Belrive with Elizabeth and his devoted friend Henry Clerval, contrasting Elizabeth's poetic calm and Clerval's chivalric ambition with his own vehement thirst to learn the secrets of heaven and earth.

muse_override.reason: Idyllic harmonious childhood filled with calm joy and wonder at nature's sublime mysteries.

scenes.title: The Fatal Thirst for Forbidden Knowledge
scenes.summary: Looking back with foreboding, Victor traces his ruin to age thirteen, when his father's dismissive rejection of Cornelius Agrippa only inflamed his obsession with ancient alchemy, the elixir of life, and the raising of ghosts.

muse_override.reason: Nostalgic childhood wonder curdling into obsessive thirst for alchemy, ghosts, and the elixir of life.

scenes.title: Thunderstorm and the Shattered Oak
scenes.summary: At fifteen, Victor watches a violent thunderstorm shatter an oak to ribbons, and a visiting philosopher's explanation of electricity and galvanism suddenly topples his occult idols and fills him with disdain for natural philosophy.

scenes.title: False Peace Before Doom
scenes.summary: Victor experiences a brief guardian-angel tranquility after abandoning science for mathematics, only to conclude bitterly that destiny had already decreed his utter destruction.

scenes.title: The Mother's Sacrifice
scenes.summary: On the eve of Victor's departure for Ingolstadt, Elizabeth falls gravely ill with scarlet fever. Caroline nurses her back to life at the cost of her own, dying after joining Elizabeth's and Victor's hands and blessing their future union. The household is plunged into first, irreparable grief.

scenes.title: Mourning and Farewell
scenes.summary: Departure is deferred for mourning. Elizabeth veils her sorrow to comfort the family. On the final evening Henry Clerval, denied his own wish to study, bids Victor farewell, and at dawn father, Elizabeth, and Clerval see him off to the carriage.

scenes.title: Alone on the Road to Ingolstadt
scenes.summary: Alone for the first time, Victor leaves home in melancholy, dreading strangers and life without family and friends, but his spirits rise as travel awakens his ambition to gain knowledge and take his place in the world.

scenes.title: First Meeting with Krempe
scenes.summary: Victor arrives in Ingolstadt and visits the professors, first meeting the uncouth natural philosophy professor M. Krempe, who stares in disbelief when Victor names the alchemists as his principal studies.

muse_override.reason: Tense academic dismissal after lonely arrival creates suspense and mystery with faint adventure.

scenes.title: Rebuff and Contempt for Modern Science
scenes.summary: Krempe scornfully condemns Victor's alchemical books as wasted, exploded nonsense and orders him to begin anew, leaving Victor undismayed but repelled by both teacher and modern science's petty realities compared to grand alchemical dreams.

muse_override.reason: Disdainful dismissal crushes grand alchemical dreams into disappointed contempt.

scenes.title: Waldman's Electrifying Lecture
scenes.summary: Drawn by curiosity about the kindly Professor Waldman, Victor attends his chemistry lecture. Waldman's fervent panegyric on modern masters who command lightning and reveal nature's hiding-places strikes Victor like fate, awakening a single consuming purpose to pioneer creation's mysteries.

scenes.title: Resolution of Destiny
scenes.summary: Sleepless with turmoil, Victor resolves to return to science and visits Waldman, who receives him with mild encouragement, validates past genius, and advises broad study. Shown the laboratory and given guidance, Victor closes a day that decides his destiny.

muse_override.reason: Calm resolution at dawn and hopeful mentorship bring wonder at a new scientific destiny.

scenes.title: Ardent Study and Rapid Progress
scenes.summary: Victor devotes himself wholly to chemistry and natural philosophy at Ingolstadt, guided by Waldman and Krempe, progressing so rapidly for two years that he improves chemical instruments and considers returning home.

scenes.title: Discovery of the Secret of Life
scenes.summary: Obsessed with the principle of life, Victor haunts vaults, charnel-houses, and anatomy rooms until a brilliant breakthrough reveals the cause of generation, filling him with delight and rapture at reaching the summit of his desires.

scenes.title: Resolution and Secret Toil
scenes.summary: Refusing to reveal the secret and warning Walton against dangerous ambition, Victor resolves to create a gigantic human being and labors in his solitary workshop amid bones and corruption, driven by visionary hubris and frantic, loathsome toil.

scenes.title: Summer Pursuit and Neglected Affections
scenes.summary: Through a beautiful summer Victor remains wholly absorbed in his work, insensible to nature and neglecting absent friends, recalling his father's warning that interrupted correspondence proves other duties neglected.

scenes.title: Moral Reflection and Anxious Decline
scenes.summary: Victor cannot tear himself from his loathsome yet irresistible employment, moralizes that no study justifying loss of tranquillity and domestic affection is lawful, then describes winter approaching as fever, nervousness, and guilt-like seclusion mark his physical decline near completion.

scenes.title: The Spark of Life and Horror
scenes.summary: On a dreary November night Victor animates the creature and is overcome by horror and disgust at its yellow eye and hideous contrast. He flees his workshop, suffers feverish nightmares of Elizabeth turning to his dead mother, and wakes to find the monster at his bedside grinning and reaching for him, driving him to hide in the courtyard.

scenes.title: A Wretched Night and Lonely Wandering
scenes.summary: Alone through the night and into a dismal wet morning, Victor reflects on his ruined dreams and complete overthrow. He wanders the streets of Ingolstadt in sick fear, unable to return home, haunted by the sense of a frightful fiend treading behind him.

scenes.title: Clerval's Joyful Arrival
scenes.summary: At the diligence stop Victor unexpectedly meets his friend Henry Clerval. Overjoyed and momentarily forgetting his horror, he welcomes Clerval with calm joy, hears news of family in Geneva, but betrays his illness and exhausted, overworked state.

scenes.title: The Empty Room and Collapse
scenes.summary: Trembling with dread that the creature is still in his apartment and that Henry will see it, Victor rushes upstairs to find the rooms empty and rejoices. Back with Clerval his relief collapses into wild laughter and hysteria as he imagines the spectre returning, and he falls down in a fit.

scenes.title: Nervous Fever and Spring Convalescence
scenes.summary: Victor sinks into a months-long nervous fever nursed solely by Henry, who conceals its severity from Victor's family. Haunted by the monster, Victor raves incessantly until, by slow degrees amid divine spring, his cheerfulness revives.

muse_override.reason: Slow recovery into divine spring restores joy and calm after fevered raving.

scenes.title: Gratitude and a Letter from Home
scenes.summary: Victor thanks Henry for sacrificing his winter to nurse him. Henry gently urges him to write home to reassure his father and cousin, then presents a letter from his cousin that has been waiting for him.

muse_override.reason: Warm convalescent gratitude and relief outweigh a brief anxious tremor about home.

scenes.title: A Plea for One Word in His Own Hand
scenes.summary: Clerval hands Victor a letter from Elizabeth. She writes that he has been very ill, that Henry's letters cannot reassure her, and begs for one word in his own hand. She urges him to get well and return to a happy home, reports his father is well, describes Ernest at sixteen as active but averse to study and wanting foreign military service, and begins Justine Moritz's history, her mother's cruelty, and her reception into the Frankenstein house.

scenes.title: Justine the Grateful Favorite
scenes.summary: Elizabeth recalls Justine as Victor's great favourite, frank-hearted and happy, beloved by her aunt Caroline, who gave her a superior education. Justine repaid it with silent, devoted gratitude, imitating her protectress in phrase and manners.

scenes.title: Grief, Blame, and Return
scenes.summary: Elizabeth recounts Justine's later trials: neglect after her aunt's death, illness, the successive deaths of her brothers and sister, and recall by her repentant Catholic mother who blamed her for their deaths. After Madame Moritz died at the beginning of last winter, Justine returned to Geneva, clever, gentle, pretty, and tenderly loved.

scenes.title: William, Gossip, and Farewell Entreaty
scenes.summary: Elizabeth closes with news of little William, his looks and child sweethearts, and Geneva gossip about the Mansfield sisters' marriages and Louis Manoir's misfortunes and expected marriage. She thanks Henry, renews her anxious plea for Victor to write even one line, and signs from Geneva, March 18th.

muse_override.reason: Warm domestic letter brightened by William and light gossip, tinged with closing anxious affection.

scenes.title: Convalescence and the Torture of Praise
scenes.summary: Roused by Elizabeth's letter, Victor writes home and steadily recovers enough to leave his chamber. When he introduces Clerval to the professors, Waldman's kind praise of his scientific progress and Krempe's blunt encomiums renew his agony and dread of natural philosophy, which Clerval tactfully deflects.

scenes.title: Consolation in Oriental Studies
scenes.summary: To escape reflection, Victor joins Clerval in studying Persian, Arabic, and Sanskrit, finding instruction and soothing consolation in orientalist poetry.

scenes.title: A Delayed Return and Farewell Tour
scenes.summary: Summer passes and Victor's return to Geneva is delayed by winter snows until spring; in May, Henry proposes a farewell pedestrian tour around Ingolstadt before departure.

scenes.title: A Healed Heart on the Walking Tour
scenes.summary: Victor and Henry spend a fortnight walking in the countryside. Salubrious air, nature, and Clerval's imagination and affection restore Victor's health, gaiety, and love of the world. They return on a bright Sunday to dancing peasants, with Victor bounding in unbridled joy.

scenes.title: The Fatal Letter from Geneva
scenes.summary: Victor receives his father's letter preparing him for terrible news: William has been murdered in Plainpalais, Elizabeth blames herself over a stolen miniature, and Alphonse begs Victor to return home to comfort them without vengeance.

scenes.title: Despair and Farewell
scenes.summary: Shattered by the letter, Victor weeps while Clerval reads and sympathizes. Victor resolves to leave for Geneva at once, listens to Clerval's mournful consolation on William's rest, and hurries off alone in a cabriolet.

scenes.title: The Melancholy Return
scenes.summary: Victor's melancholy journey home slows with dread near familiar scenes. After two days of calm reflection at Lausanne, the sight of his mountains and lake briefly delights him before grief and dark foreboding close in as night falls.

scenes.title: Storm and Terrible Revelation
scenes.summary: Unable to enter Geneva at night, Victor crosses to Plainpalais in a violent thunderstorm. Amid lightning he sees his gigantic creation, realizes with horror that it murdered William, and spends the wet night tormented by guilt for loosing a vampire upon the world.

scenes.title: Resolve to Stay Silent
scenes.summary: At dawn Victor hastens toward Geneva intending to denounce the murderer, but reflects that his tale of creating a living being met on an inaccessible precipice will sound like delirium and that pursuit of a creature able to scale Mont Saleve would be useless, so he resolves to remain silent.

scenes.title: Reunion in the Library
scenes.summary: About five in the morning Victor enters his father's house, waits in the library among family portraits, and tearfully reunites with Ernest, who tells him of their desolated home, their sinking father, Elizabeth's self-accusation, and lost William.

scenes.title: The Accusation of Justine
scenes.summary: Ernest reveals the supposed murderer has been found: Justine Moritz, in whose pocket Caroline's miniature was discovered after William's murder, leading to her apprehension. Victor reacts in disbelief and protests that the accusation must be wrongful.

scenes.title: The Hope of Acquittal
scenes.summary: Victor insists Justine is innocent and claims secret knowledge of the true murderer, which his father dismisses. Joined by Elizabeth, Victor, his father, and Elizabeth cling to hope that the trial and justice of the laws will acquit the guiltless girl.

scenes.title: Victor Suffers as Justine Faces the Court
scenes.summary: Victor accompanies his family to court in living torture, blaming his curiosity for William's death and Justine's impending doom, while Justine appears calm and beautiful in mourning, constrained yet confident in innocence before a hostile crowd.

scenes.title: Witnesses Testify Against Justine
scenes.summary: The prosecution opens and witnesses testify against Justine: out all night near where William's body was found, confused when questioned, hysterical at the sight of the body, and found with William's miniature in her pocket, identified by Elizabeth to murmurs of horror.

scenes.title: Justine's Innocent Plea
scenes.summary: Called to defend herself, Justine calmly explains spending the night searching for William and sleeping in a barn, but cannot explain how the picture came to be in her pocket and commits her cause to her judges.

scenes.title: Elizabeth Defends Justine
scenes.summary: After character witnesses speak timidly for Justine, Elizabeth insists on addressing the court and passionately vouches for Justine's amiable, devoted character and perfect innocence.

scenes.title: Victor Flees in Remorse
scenes.summary: Elizabeth's appeal wins admiration but not sympathy for Justine, and Victor, certain his creature murdered William and doomed Justine, rushes from the court in remorseful agony.

scenes.title: Condemnation and False Confession
scenes.summary: Victor learns the ballots were all black and Justine is condemned, and is stunned to hear she has confessed; Elizabeth is crushed in her faith in goodness, then insists Victor accompany her to visit Justine in prison.

scenes.title: Farewell in the Prison Cell
scenes.summary: In the prison cell, Justine weeps at Elizabeth's feet and admits she falsely confessed under her confessor's threats of hell; Elizabeth begs forgiveness and vows to save her, while Victor hides his guilt as Justine finds resigned courage and bids farewell.

scenes.title: Execution and Remorse
scenes.summary: Justine dies on the scaffold despite all appeals; Victor is consumed by hellish remorse, mourning the grief he has brought on Elizabeth, his father, and his home, and foreboding more deaths to come.

scenes.title: Remorse and a Father's Consolation
scenes.summary: In the aftermath of Justine's death, Victor is consumed by guilt, remorse, and sleepless despair. He shuns human company for dark solitude while his father urges stoic fortitude for the sake of survivors, advice rendered useless by Victor's hidden secret terror.

scenes.title: Mourning at Belrive
scenes.summary: Retired to Belrive, the household lives as a house of mourning. Victor rows alone at night on the lake, tempted by suicide but restrained by love for Elizabeth and his family, and burning with hatred and revenge toward the monster. Elizabeth mourns Justine's innocence and shaken faith in justice, tries tenderly to comfort Victor, but neither friendship nor beauty can pierce his cloud of woe.

scenes.title: Despairing Journey Toward Chamounix
scenes.summary: Driven by sullen despair, Victor abruptly leaves home for the valley of Chamounix. Travelling by horse and then mule through the ravine of Arve, he is lightened by the sublime precipices, raging river, waterfalls, and towering Alps and Mont Blanc.

scenes.title: Fleeting Relief and Sleep at Chamounix
scenes.summary: On the road Victor feels fleeting boyhood pleasure at familiar sights, quickly fettered again by horror and despair. Exhausted in body and mind, he reaches Chamounix and finds oblivion in sleep to the rushing Arve beneath Mont Blanc.

scenes.title: Consolation Among the Glaciers
scenes.summary: Victor roams the valley by the sources of the Arveiron beneath the glacier and vast mountains. The sublime, solemn scene subdues and tranquillises his grief and brings him peaceful sleep among grand natural shapes.

scenes.title: Melancholy Ascent in Rain
scenes.summary: Waking to pouring rain, mists, and dark melancholy, Victor resolves to ascend Montanvert alone for solemn relief. He climbs the precipitous, avalanche-scarred, desolate path, reflecting gloomily on human sensibility and mutability.

scenes.title: Joy on the Sea of Ice
scenes.summary: Reaching the summit near noon, Victor crosses the uneven sea of ice as the mist clears. Gazing on Mont Blanc in awful majesty, his sorrowful heart swells with joy and he invokes wandering spirits for happiness or release.

scenes.title: Horrific Encounter and Rage
scenes.summary: The Creature suddenly appears bounding over the ice with superhuman stature. Victor is seized by horror and furious rage, reviling him as a devil and vowing combat, while the Creature reproaches his creator and threatens vengeance on his remaining friends.

scenes.title: The Creature's Entreaty for a Hearing
scenes.summary: The Creature easily eludes Victor's attack and calmly entreats him to listen, pleading his suffering, former benevolence, and lonely exclusion, and demanding justice, compassion, and a hearing before condemnation. Victor rejects him as an enemy.

muse_override.reason: Sorrowful pleading for justice dominates with tense standoff beneath.

scenes.title: The Path to the Mountain Hut
scenes.summary: Victor curses the Creature as the author of his wretchedness, but the Creature invites him to the mountain hut to hear his tale. Moved by curiosity, compassion, doubt over William's murder, and a sense of creator's duty, Victor reluctantly follows across the ice to listen.

scenes.title: First Senses in the Forest
scenes.summary: The Creature awakens confused by overwhelming senses in the forest near Ingolstadt, learning light, dark, hunger, the moon, birdsong, and the slow sorting of sight and sound.

scenes.title: Fire Found and Kept
scenes.summary: Oppressed by cold, he finds a beggars' fire and burns his hand, learning fire both warms and hurts. He studies wood, dries wet branches, feeds and covers the fire overnight, fans it alive in the morning, and learns to cook, improving nuts and roots.

scenes.title: Fire Lost to Hunger and Snow
scenes.summary: With food scarce, he resolves to leave his dwelling despite lamenting he cannot reproduce his fire. Wrapping in his cloak, he travels three days toward the setting sun and emerges into a cold, uniform white open country covered in fresh snow.

scenes.title: Fright at the Hut
scenes.summary: At dawn the Creature finds an open shepherd's hut, frightening its old occupant into shrieking flight. Enchanted by dry shelter, he devours the shepherd's bread, cheese, and milk and falls asleep in the straw.

muse_override.reason: Creature's wonder at shelter clashes with shepherd's terrified flight.

scenes.title: Stoned from the Village
scenes.summary: Waking at noon, the Creature walks to a village and enters a cottage for food, but children shriek and the villagers attack him with stones. Bruised and driven off, he takes refuge in a low, bare wooden hovel.

muse_override.reason: Wonder at the village turns to violent rejection, stoning, and fearful refuge in a bare hovel.

scenes.title: Sanctuary Behind the Cottage
scenes.summary: He hides in the low shed behind a cottage, secures it for shelter and warmth, and watches a sad young woman and despondent young man pass with milk and tools.

muse_override.reason: Shelter brings warm relief and quiet observation tinged with melancholy.

scenes.title: Watching Through the Chink
scenes.summary: Peering through a chink, he watches the cottagers' music, tears, meals, tapers, and evening reading with overpowering pain and pleasure until they extinguish their lights to rest.

scenes.title: Night Watch and Morning Routine
scenes.summary: The Creature lies awake resolving to stay hidden while studying the cottagers. He watches their gentle morning routine and loving devotion to the blind old man, but is troubled by the unexplained weeping of Felix and Agatha amid apparent comfort.

muse_override.reason: Quiet nocturnal watching and tender domestic routine mixed with loneliness and unexplained tears.

scenes.title: The Discovery of Poverty
scenes.summary: He discovers the family's uneasiness is grinding poverty and hunger, living only on garden vegetables and little milk, with the younger cottagers going without for the old man. Moved by their kindness, he stops stealing their stores and subsists on berries, nuts, and roots.

scenes.title: The Invisible Helper
scenes.summary: He begins secretly helping by taking the youth's tools at night and bringing home several days' worth of firewood. The young woman and youth are astonished to find the pile in the morning, and the youth spends the day repairing the cottage and garden instead of gathering wood.

muse_override.reason: Quiet secret kindness brings warm joy and wonder with a soft mysterious night feel.

scenes.title: Learning Speech in Winter
scenes.summary: Over months he painstakingly learns articulate language - fire, milk, bread, Felix, Agatha, father - and grows deeply attached through winter, puzzling over reading and longing to master speech before revealing himself.

scenes.title: Horror at His Own Reflection
scenes.summary: The creature sees his own deformed reflection in a transparent pool and is filled with despondence and mortification. As winter ends the snow vanishes, famine among the cottagers fades, and they find sufficient wholesome food with new plants in the garden.

scenes.title: The Invisible Good Spirit
scenes.summary: The old man walks daily leaning on his son as the season grows pleasant. The creature settles into a uniform hidden life, observing by day and gathering food and fuel by night while secretly doing chores for the cottage, labours the family marvels at as those of a good spirit.

scenes.title: Dreams of Acceptance in Spring
scenes.summary: He dreams of winning their love with gentle words despite his figure, and applies himself to language with renewed hope as spring's warmth, birds, and budding nature lift his spirits with anticipations of joy.

scenes.title: The Veiled Visitor
scenes.summary: The Creature turns to the more moving part of his tale as spring blooms into beauty. He watches the cottagers rest to the old man's guitar and notes Felix's deep melancholy. A veiled lady on horseback arrives asking for Felix, then lifts her veil to reveal angelic beauty.

scenes.title: Safie's Welcome and Joy Restored
scenes.summary: Felix is transformed with ecstatic joy at the stranger, kissing her hand as his sweet Arabian and leading her into the cottage where her presence diffuses gladness. That night her name is revealed as Safie, and the next morning her entrancing guitar and song, followed by Agatha's sweet air, replace sadness with peaceable joy while the Creature profits in learning language.

scenes.title: Lessons in Language and History
scenes.summary: With joy restored, the Creature devotes his days to secretly learning language alongside Safie, outpacing her. He learns letters and through Felix's reading of Volney's Ruins of Empires gains a cursory knowledge of history, empires, manners, governments, and religions.

scenes.title: Knowledge Turns to Despair
scenes.summary: Knowledge turns to anguish as the Creature reflects on human virtue and vice, wealth and rank, and realizes he has no money, friends, lineage, or fellow being, and a hideous form. Overwhelmed by sorrow, isolation, and questions of his origin and family, he feels shut out from the cottagers he loves and reveres.

scenes.title: A Noble Family Ruined
scenes.summary: The Creature introduces the affecting history of the cottagers: the respected, affluent De Lacey family in Paris, ruined by the unjust condemnation of a Turkish merchant.

scenes.title: Felix's Vow and Promise of Safie
scenes.summary: Felix witnesses the unjust trial and vows to free the Turkish prisoner, contacting him through his dungeon grate. Moved by Safie's gratitude and beauty, he is promised her hand in marriage, and his zeal is further warmed by grateful letters from Safie written with help in French.

muse_override.reason: Secret prison plot with solemn vow and budding love blends tense suspense with romantic adventure.

scenes.title: Safie's Mother and Dread of the Harem
scenes.summary: The creature summarizes Safie's letters, recounting how her Christian Arab mother, enslaved and married by the Turk, taught her religion, intellect, and independence of spirit. Safie dreads return to Asia and the harem, and longs to marry a Christian and remain where women hold rank in society.

muse_override.reason: Mournful slavery and loss tempered by defiant hope against harem confinement.

scenes.title: Escape to Italy and Young Love
scenes.summary: On the eve of execution Felix smuggles the Turk from prison to Lyons and Leghorn, lingering in tender, hopeful intimacy with Safie on promise of marriage.

scenes.title: The Turk's Secret Treachery
scenes.summary: The Turk encourages the intimacy between Felix and Safie while secretly loathing a union with a Christian and plotting to prolong the deceit until he can flee with his daughter, aided by news arriving from Paris.

muse_override.reason: Secret plotting and prolonged deceit create tense suspense and mystery.

scenes.title: Sacrifice and Exile
scenes.summary: Felix nobly surrenders in Paris to save his imprisoned father and sister, but fails to free them as they lose their fortune and are exiled to the German cottage, while the ungrateful Turk flees Italy with Safie.

scenes.title: Felix's Misery and the Tyrannical Order
scenes.summary: Felix is left miserable by the Turk's ingratitude and the loss of Safie, until her arrival revives him. At Leghorn, Safie's father orders her to forget Felix and prepare to return to Turkey, outraging her generous nature.

scenes.title: Safie's Flight to the Cottage
scenes.summary: Warned of discovery, the Turk plans to sail for Constantinople and leave Safie behind. Abhorring Turkey, she takes jewels and money and flees toward Germany with an attendant, who dies near the cottage, leaving Safie to be guided safely to her lover.

scenes.title: A Treasure in the Woods
scenes.summary: The Creature reflects on the cottagers' history with admiration and a desire to join human society, then finds a lost portmanteau in the woods containing clothes and three books that delight him.

muse_override.reason: Quiet nighttime discovery of books brings wonder, gentle joy and mystery.

scenes.title: Werther, Plutarch, and the Torment of Identity
scenes.summary: The Creature describes how Werther filled him with ecstasy and dejection and sympathy for gentle domestic virtue, and how Plutarch's Lives lifted him toward admiration of heroes and peaceable lawgivers, while forcingTormenting questions of who and what he is, whence he came, and what his fate must be.

muse_override.reason: Melancholic identity torment and dejection fused with astonished wonder at Werther and Plutarch's heroes.

scenes.title: Paradise Lost and the Horror of Creation
scenes.summary: Paradise Lost moves the Creature as true history, leaving him torn between lonely Adam and envious Satan, and reading Victor's laboratory journal reveals his accursed origin and loathsome form in his creator's own horrified words, filling him with sickness and rage at his solitude.

scenes.title: Resolve Not to Despair
scenes.summary: The Creature resolves not to despair, persuading himself the cottagers' benevolence will outweigh his deformity, and postpones revealing himself for months to improve his understanding.

muse_override.reason: Fragile hope tempers despondency with anxious dread before the fateful interview.

scenes.title: Autumn Longing and Horror
scenes.summary: As Safie brings happiness and plenty to the cottage, the Creature feels ever more wretched and alone, horrified by his reflection, yet watches autumn fade and yearns increasingly for the cottagers' kindness and protection.

scenes.title: Plan to Approach Alone
scenes.summary: With winter completing a year of life, the Creature fixes his plan to approach the blind old De Lacey alone, hoping his voice will win mediation before the others see his hideous form.

scenes.title: Plea to the Blind Father
scenes.summary: Finding De Lacey alone playing mournful music, the Creature overcomes terror to enter, pleads as a lonely traveller, and draws tender encouragement and an offer of help from the blind old man.

scenes.title: Hope Shattered by Violence
scenes.summary: As the Creature seizes De Lacey's hand for protection, Felix, Safie, and Agatha return; in horror Felix tears him away and beats him, and the Creature flees in anguish to his hovel.

muse_override.reason: Desperate hope collapses into violent rejection, blending sorrow, fear, and physical assault.

scenes.title: Rage in the Night Wood
scenes.summary: Rejected and enraged, the Creature flees into the night wood, howling like a wild beast, sinking into despair and declaring everlasting war against mankind and his creator.

scenes.title: resolve to Return
scenes.summary: Hiding until daylight, the Creature calms, reproaches himself for hasty exposure, resolves to win old De Lacey alone, then sleeps feverishly haunted by Felix tearing him away.

scenes.title: The Deserted Cottage
scenes.summary: Returning to the silent cottage, the Creature waits in anguish then overhears Felix renounce the home in horror, realizing the De Laceys have abandoned him forever.

scenes.title: Fire and Vengeance
scenes.summary: Consumed by hatred and grief, the Creature destroys the garden, waits for the moon to set, then dances in insane fury as he sets the cottage ablaze before fleeing to the woods.

scenes.title: Journey Toward the Creator
scenes.summary: Homeless, the Creature resolves to seek his creator in Geneva for justice, enduring a long, freezing autumn journey southward as revenge hardens within him.

scenes.title: Spring Briefly Softens the Outcast
scenes.summary: Travelling by day through a deep wood in early spring, the Creature is briefly revived to gentleness, pleasure, and thankful tears by sunshine and balmy air, forgetting his solitude and deformity.

scenes.title: Rescue Rewarded with a Bullet
scenes.summary: At a rapid river the Creature saves a laughing girl who slips and falls in, but when a rustic rushes up he tears her from the Creature's arms, flees, and shoots the Creature when followed.

scenes.title: Pain Turns Gentleness to Vengeance
scenes.summary: Writhing from his shattered shoulder, the Creature's kindness turns to hellish rage and vows of eternal vengeance, then he faints and spends weeks miserably in the woods nursing the wound and brooding on injustice.

scenes.title: Arrival at Geneva
scenes.summary: Healed but joyless, the Creature presses on, reaching the environs of Geneva at evening and hiding in the fields to plan how to confront his maker.

scenes.title: Murder of the Child
scenes.summary: Seizing a beautiful unprejudiced child as a future companion, the Creature is enraged when William curses him as monster and Frankenstein, strangling him as his first victim in exultant triumph.

scenes.title: The Framed Portrait and Demand
scenes.summary: Gazing on the murdered boy's miniature, the Creature's rage returns; he frames a sleeping young woman with the portrait, then haunts the mountains demanding Victor create a mate like himself.

muse_override.reason: Cold confession of framing and looming demand breeds tense dread with tragic undercurrent.

scenes.title: A Demand Refused
scenes.summary: The Creature demands a female companion as his right. Victor, his anger rekindled, flatly refuses to create another being.

scenes.title: Threat of Inextinguishable Hatred
scenes.summary: The Creature answers with menacing rage, vowing inextinguishable hatred and Victor's destruction if love is denied, his face contorted before he calms.

muse_override.reason: Direct vow of inextinguishable hatred and destruction creates confrontational dread tinged with misery.

scenes.title: A Reasonable Demand
scenes.summary: The Creature reasons with Victor, asking for a mate as hideous as himself as a moderate and reasonable request that would make his exile harmless and content.

scenes.title: Promise of Peaceful Exile
scenes.summary: Victor is moved to pity by the Creature's justice and fine feelings, as the Creature promises peaceful exile in South America and begs him to consent out of compassion.

scenes.title: Oaths and Doubts
scenes.summary: Victor objects that exile cannot hold and distrusts him; the Creature swears to quit mankind forever and argues companionship will end his vice.

scenes.title: The Fateful Promise
scenes.summary: After weighing justice, power, and threats, Victor consents on oath of eternal exile. The Creature swears never to return and vanishes down the mountain.

scenes.title: Descent in Darkness
scenes.summary: Alone at sunset, Victor descends slowly in heavy grief, weeps by the fountain under the stars, and returns haggard to Geneva resolved to his abhorred task.

scenes.title: Melancholy Return to Geneva
scenes.summary: Back in Geneva, Victor avoids his promise to create a female, sinking into melancholy relieved only by solitary boating, until his father draws him aside with a grave conjecture.

muse_override.reason: Lingering guilt and melancholy briefly soothed by solitary lake calm shifts to fearful tension as father confronts him.

scenes.title: A Father's Fear of Another Love
scenes.summary: Alphonse confesses he had looked forward to Victor's marriage to Elizabeth, but fears Victor loves another and feels bound in honour, causing his misery.

scenes.title: A Profession of Love and Immediate Marriage
scenes.summary: Victor professes tender love for Elizabeth, and his delighted father proposes an immediate marriage as cure for his gloom, without wishing to dictate to him.

muse_override.reason: Tender love and hopeful marriage bring joy and calm shadowed by lingering gloom and suspense.

scenes.title: Secret Resolve for England
scenes.summary: Alone with his horror, Victor resolves he must fulfill his dread engagement first, conceals his true motive to obtain leave for England, accepts Clerval as companion, and agonizes over leaving friends exposed to the fiend.

scenes.title: Farewell and Reunion at Strasburg
scenes.summary: Victor tearfully leaves Geneva with his instruments, travels in listless indifference to Strasburg, and is joined by joyful Clerval, a stark contrast to his own despondency.

scenes.title: Down the Picturesque Rhine
scenes.summary: Descending the Rhine past castles, vineyards, and vintage songs, even depressed Victor drinks in tranquillity while Henry rhapsodizes that this divine river surpasses Switzerland.

scenes.title: Elegy for Beloved Henry
scenes.summary: The narrative pauses for a retrospective lament, quoting Wordsworth to celebrate Clerval's poetic nature and mourning his gentle spirit as lost yet still consoling.

scenes.title: Across Holland to London
scenes.summary: Past Cologne the scenery dulls, the travelers post to Rotterdam and sail to England, sighting the white cliffs, the Thames towns, and at last the steeples of London.

muse_override.reason: Steady travel culminating in wondrous first sight of England evokes adventure and awe.

scenes.title: London in Gloom
scenes.summary: In London, Victor seeks only scientific information to fulfill his promise while brooding over William and Justine. Clerval delights in genius and society, highlighting Victor's isolation, guilt, and anguish as he begins collecting materials for the new creation.

scenes.title: London Plans - Northern Tour Resolved
scenes.summary: After months in London, Victor and Clerval receive an invitation to Perth and decide to extend their tour north via Windsor, Oxford, Matlock, and the Cumberland lakes, Victor packing his instruments to finish his labours in Scotland.

scenes.title: Windsor and Oxford - History Admired
scenes.summary: Leaving London on March 27th, they ramble through Windsor's majestic forest, then enter Oxford, admiring its ancient colleges, magnificent streets, and placid Isis while tracing memories of Charles I and the Civil War.

scenes.title: Oxford Environs - Beauty Embittered
scenes.summary: Amid Oxford's environs and monuments to liberty like Hampden's tomb, Victor feels momentary elevation to free and lofty contemplation, then sinks back as a blasted, hopeless wreck, embittered by past and future.

scenes.title: Northward Through Matlock to Edinburgh
scenes.summary: Journeying through Matlock and the Cumberland lakes to Edinburgh, Victor is briefly cheated toward happiness by familiar Swiss-like scenery. Dread returns with thoughts of his neglected promise, fear that the daemon will murder Henry or his family, and impatient longing to be alone.

scenes.title: Separation in Scotland
scenes.summary: At Perth Victor refuses society and begs Clerval to let him tour Scotland alone for a month or two. Henry reluctantly consents, and Victor resolves to finish his work in solitude, convinced the monster follows him to claim his companion.

scenes.title: The Remote Orkney Hut
scenes.summary: Victor settles on a barren rock in the remotest Orkneys, hiring a squalid ruined hut among five impoverished inhabitants. He labours in the mornings and walks the roaring, desolate beach in the evenings, contrasting the giant ocean with gentle Switzerland.

scenes.title: The Detestable Labour
scenes.summary: The work becomes filthy and horrible in cold blood, unlike his first blinded frenzy. Isolated and restless, Victor toils fitfully, sickened at heart, fearing at every moment to meet his persecutor while trembling between eager hope of completion and forebodings of evil.

scenes.title: Moral Reckoning in the Lab
scenes.summary: Alone in his island laboratory at moonrise, Victor pauses work on the female creature and reasons through the horror of his promise: she might reject the compact, mate hatred, or spawn a race of devils that imperils all mankind.

scenes.title: Destruction at the Casement
scenes.summary: The Creature grins at the casement watching his progress; maddened by malice and treachery in its face, Victor tears apart the unfinished female, suffers its howl of revenge, then locks the room vowing never to resume.

scenes.title: Night Intrusion
scenes.summary: Gazing at the still moonlit sea, Victor hears oars land and his door creak; paralyzed with presentiment, he hears footsteps approach until the dreaded wretch opens his chamber door.

scenes.title: Broken Promise and Defiant Refusal
scenes.summary: The Creature reproaches Victor for destroying the half-finished mate after months of toil through Germany, England, and Scotland, and demands he keep his promise. Victor refuses to create another being equal in deformity and wickedness. The Creature drops entreaty, claims power as Victor's master, and orders obedience, but Victor declares his irresolution past and refuses to loose a daemon upon the earth.

scenes.title: Revenge Vowed and the Wedding-Night Threat
scenes.summary: Seeing Victor firm, the Creature curses him to dread and misery, vowing revenge dearer than light or food and promising to watch with a snake's wiliness. Victor calls him Devil and declares himself inexorable. The Creature departs with the threat to be with him on his wedding-night, and Victor defiantly warns him to ensure his own safety.

scenes.title: Aftermath Rage and Dread
scenes.summary: The Creature escapes by boat across the waves; left in silence, Victor burns with rage, imagines future victims, and weeps for Elizabeth as he fixes on the wedding-night as his fated death.

scenes.title: Dawn Despair and Lifeline
scenes.summary: At dawn Victor wanders the beach in despair, sleeps on the grass to calm his nerves, then receives letters from Geneva and Clerval urging him to leave the isle and meet at Perth.

scenes.title: Clearing the Lab and Sea Burial
scenes.summary: Resolved that creating another fiend would be base selfishness, Victor clears his odious laboratory, packs the mangled remains with stones, and under moon and cloud casts them into the sea before drifting asleep in his skiff.

muse_override.reason: Secret night burial of horrific remains blends dread-filled suspense and mystery with fleeting uneasy calm.

scenes.title: Adrift Without Compass
scenes.summary: Awaking far offshore with a high northeast wind and no compass, Victor drifts helplessly before the wind, tormented by thirst, fear of starvation and drowning in the Atlantic, and despair over Elizabeth, his father, and Clerval left exposed to the monster.

scenes.title: Sight of Land and Harbor Entry
scenes.summary: As the wind dies and the sea calms, Victor sights high land to the south, fashions a sail from his clothing, steers toward cultivated shore with vessels, steeple, and harbor town, and enters joyfully to seek nourishment.

scenes.title: Accused Stranger Ashore
scenes.summary: Surrounded by a curious and angry English-speaking crowd, Victor is rudely seized, learns from a magistrate's man that he must answer for a gentleman found murdered the night before, and follows exhausted toward Mr. Kirwin's house.

scenes.title: Testimony of the Drowned Man
scenes.summary: Before a calm but severe magistrate, a fisherman testifies how he stumbled on the body of a handsome young man, apparently strangled, with finger marks on his neck and clothes dry and warm.

scenes.title: The Lone Boat Seen
scenes.summary: Victor trembles at the strangling mark, recalling William, while Daniel Nugent and shore women swear they saw a lone boat like his near where the corpse was found, implying he returned the body to shore.

scenes.title: The Coffin Reveal
scenes.summary: Led to the inn to view the corpse, Victor discovers it is Henry Clerval and collapses in horror and guilt, crying that his machinations have killed again.

scenes.title: Fever and the Dungeon Awakening
scenes.summary: Convulsions give way to two months of fever and raving about William, Justine, Clerval and the fiend; Victor laments surviving, then wakes bewildered in a barred prison cell.

scenes.title: The Cold Nursing
scenes.summary: Watched by a hard, indifferent hired nurse and a careless physician, Victor feels the loneliness of a condemned murderer, learning only later of Mr. Kirwin's quiet kindness in housing and treating him.

scenes.title: A Sympathetic Visit
scenes.summary: While Victor sits in gloomy despair, Mr. Kirwin enters with sympathy and tries to comfort him, recounting his shocking arrest and Clerval's murder, which surprises Victor by how much Kirwin knows about him.

scenes.title: A Father Arrives
scenes.summary: Kirwin explains he found Victor's papers and wrote to Geneva, then announces a visiting friend; Victor first panics that it is the monster come to mock him, then rejoices to learn it is his father, who enters the room.

scenes.title: Father's Arrival and Grief
scenes.summary: Victor's father arrives like a good angel, calming him with news of home, but mention of Clerval undoes him; he sinks into black melancholy haunted by his friend's ghastly image.

scenes.title: Acquitted into Darkness
scenes.summary: After three months in prison Victor is taken to the assizes, but Mr. Kirwin's defence proves he was in Orkney when Clerval was found, so the bill is rejected and he is freed. His father rejoices, but Victor feels no relief, haunted by Henry's dying eyes and the monster's watery eyes, sunk in torpor and restrained from suicide. Only duty to return to Geneva to guard his loved ones and kill the monster rouses him, and despite his shattered health they sail from Ireland at midnight while he weeps over his ruined life.

scenes.title: Fiend's Grasp in Sleep
scenes.summary: Aboard the vessel, Victor takes a double dose of his nightly laudanum to rest, but sleep brings terrifying dreams culminating in a nightmare of the fiend's grasp at his neck amid groans. His watching father wakes him to dashing waves and cloudy sky, the fiend absent, granting a brief truce-like calm and forgetfulness.

scenes.title: Despair in Paris
scenes.summary: In Paris Victor collapses in guilt and exhaustion, shunning society as unworthy after unleashing a murderous enemy. His father tries to comfort him as pride or delirium, but Victor insists he murdered William, Justine, and Henry and hides the full secret of the creature for fear of seeming mad.

scenes.title: A Letter from Geneva
scenes.summary: Elizabeth writes from Geneva, joyful that Victor is near Paris and soon to return, but troubled by his continued misery. She says a conversation with his father compels her to ask honestly whether he still wishes their promised marriage, or if he loves another.

muse_override.reason: Tender anxious letter holds sad suspense over whether Victor loves another.

scenes.title: An Offer of Release
scenes.summary: Elizabeth declares her love but selflessly offers to release Victor from their engagement if it is not his free choice, fearing honour binds him against his happiness. She asks him not to answer in haste and signs from Geneva.

scenes.title: The Wedding-Night Vow Remembered
scenes.summary: The letter revives the fiend's threat to be with Victor on his wedding-night. Victor interprets it as his own death sentence and a final struggle for freedom, yet resolves not to delay the marriage, and writes a calm, loving reply promising to reveal his dreadful secret the day after their union.

scenes.title: A Troubled Calm in Geneva
scenes.summary: Returned to Geneva, Victor is welcomed by Elizabeth, who is herself worn with grief. His brief calm gives way to fits of furious rage and silent torpor that only Elizabeth can soothe, while remorse denies him peace. Pressed by his father about marriage, he declares his love for Elizabeth and asks that the day be fixed.

scenes.title: A Doomed Day Fixed in Blindness
scenes.summary: Haunted by the threat 'I shall be with you on your wedding-night,' Victor regards the fiend as invincible and accepts death as no evil if balanced by losing Elizabeth. He cheerfully agrees with his father to marry in ten days, blinded to the monster's true intention and thus hastening not his own death but that of a far dearer victim.

scenes.title: Wedding Day and Departure
scenes.summary: As the wedding approaches Victor masks sinking dread with hilarity and arms himself with pistols and dagger. Elizabeth is placid but fearful, the father joyfully busy, and after the ceremony the couple embarks by water for Evian on a fair, smiling day.

scenes.title: Sheltered Beauty on the Lake
scenes.summary: Victor recalls his last moments of happiness passing rapidly on Lake Geneva, sheltered by a canopy while admiring Mont Salève, Montalègre, Mont Blanc with its snowy assemblage on one side and the dark Jura barrier on the other.

muse_override.reason: Serene lake beauty and tender love dominate, shadowed by farewell sadness and faint foreboding.

scenes.title: Sunset at Evian and Returning Dread
scenes.summary: Elizabeth tries to divert them from melancholy but fluctuates between brief joy and reverie; as the sun sinks past the Drance toward Evian and the wind falls to a breeze scented with flowers, Victor lands at sunset feeling cares and fears revive to clasp him forever.

scenes.title: Stormy Arrival and Dreadful Vigil
scenes.summary: Victor and Elizabeth land at the inn at nightfall as a violent western storm rises. Outwardly calm by day, Victor becomes anxiously watchful after dark, clutching a hidden pistol while Elizabeth trembles at his dread that this night will decide all.

scenes.title: The Scream Heard
scenes.summary: Victor patrols the passages searching for his adversary, then hears a shrill scream from Elizabeth's room and rushes toward it in horror.

scenes.title: The Lifeless Bride
scenes.summary: Victor finds Elizabeth lifeless across the bridal bed and falls senseless, then embraces her cold body and discovers the fiend's murderous mark on her neck.

scenes.title: The Fiend at the Window
scenes.summary: Looking up, Victor sees the monster grinning at the open window and pointing at the corpse, fires his pistol at him, and watches him escape to plunge into the lake.

scenes.title: Vain Pursuit and Crushing Grief
scenes.summary: Boats and search parties hunt the lake and woods in vain. Victor collapses in feverish exhaustion, then mourns over Elizabeth's corpse in bewildered grief. Haunted by the deaths of William, Justine, and Clerval, he rows back toward Geneva through rain, crushed by sudden, total loss.

scenes.title: Geneva Desolation and Vow of Revenge
scenes.summary: Victor returns to Geneva to find his father and Ernest alive, but his father sinks and dies in his arms under the news of Elizabeth's death. Victor loses reason, awakens in a dungeon as a supposed madman, and upon release awakens instead to a single devouring passion: revenge against the monster he created.

scenes.title: Accusation Before the Magistrate
scenes.summary: Victor accuses the creature before a Genevan criminal judge and relates his history with calm resolution; the magistrate listens with horror and interest but retreats into incredulity when called to act, calling seizure impracticable.

scenes.title: Vow of Solitary Vengeance
scenes.summary: Dismissed as delirious and soothed like a madman, Victor trembles with frenzy, declares he will devote life or death to the creature's destruction alone, and breaks angrily from the house.

scenes.title: Fury and Exile
scenes.summary: Consumed by fury and revenge after his losses, Victor abandons hateful Geneva with money and jewels and begins his ceaseless, death-haunted wandering across deserts and barbarous lands, kept alive only by vengeance.

muse_override.reason: Fury-fueled revenge and hateful exile dominate, underpinned by sorrowful wandering.

scenes.title: Silent Vigil at the Tombs
scenes.summary: After wandering aimlessly from Geneva, Victor finds himself at night at the cemetery entrance and approaches the tomb of William, Elizabeth, and his father, surrounded by silent darkness and the felt presence of the departed.

scenes.title: Oath of Vengeance Sworn
scenes.summary: Grief turns to rage as Victor kneels, kisses the earth, and swears a solemn oath by night and the spirits of vengeance to preserve his life and pursue the daemon until one of them perishes.

scenes.title: Mocking Laughter in the Moonlight
scenes.summary: A loud fiendish laugh echoes through the night, followed by the Creature's whisper of satisfaction that Victor will live on, and Victor lunges in vain as the moon reveals the monster fleeing with superhuman speed.

scenes.title: The Endless Pursuit
scenes.summary: Victor pursues the Creature for months down the Rhone to the Mediterranean and Black Sea and through Tartary and Russia, sustained by strange aid and dreams of loved ones, while taunting inscriptions urge him north to the ices.

scenes.title: To the Frozen Ocean
scenes.summary: Starved by thickening snows and frozen rivers, Victor reaches the ice-covered ocean, learns the Creature seized dogs and food and crossed the frozen sea, masters despair, and exchanges his sledge to follow onto the ice.

scenes.title: Within Grasp Then Adrift
scenes.summary: After three weeks on the ice, Victor spots the Creature's sledge and nearly closes within a mile, but the frozen sea splits with earthquake force, leaving him adrift on shrinking ice toward death until Walton's northbound ship appears and takes him aboard.

scenes.title: Swear to Satisfy My Vengeance
scenes.summary: Exhausted and fearing his task is unfulfilled, Victor begs Walton to swear to seek and kill the Creature if he survives, warning him not to trust his eloquence and to avenge William, Justine, Clerval, Elizabeth, and himself.

muse_override.reason: Dying Victor demands a vengeful oath, mixing grief, dread, and martial fury.

scenes.title: Blood Congealed by Horror
scenes.summary: Walton resumes his letter to Margaret, describing the horror of hearing Frankenstein's story, as Frankenstein alternates between suppressed tranquility, downcast wretchedness, and sudden bursts of rage and imprecation against his persecutor.

muse_override.reason: Walton recounts horror, anguish and volcanic rage shifting with suppressed sorrow.

scenes.title: Convinced Yet Denied the Secret
scenes.summary: Walton is convinced of the tale's truth more by Felix and Safie's letters and the Creature seen from the ship than by earnestness alone, but Frankenstein impenetrably rebukes his curiosity to learn the secret of creation.

scenes.title: Noble in Ruin, Living for Vengeance
scenes.summary: Frankenstein corrects Walton's notes for posterity; Walton reflects on his noble ruin, his faith that dreams are true visits from the dead, and his fallen ambition, while Frankenstein refuses new ties and declares he lives only to pursue and destroy the Creature before he dies.

scenes.title: Beset in Ice
scenes.summary: Trapped by mountains of ice with no escape, Walton fears for his men and Margaret's anxious hope, while the dying Frankenstein soothes him with cheerful auguries that briefly rouse the despairing crew.

scenes.title: Mutiny and Exhortation
scenes.summary: Facing mutiny as sailors demand a promise to turn south if freed, Walton hesitates until the enfeebled Frankenstein rises to shame them as cowards and exhort them to glory, firmness, and honour before sinking again.

scenes.title: The Promise to Return
scenes.summary: Overborne by cowardice and indecision, Walton consents to return, lamenting his blasted hopes of utility and glory as he turns toward England.

scenes.title: Death of Frankenstein
scenes.summary: As the ice breaks and the south passage opens, Frankenstein refuses return, justifies seeking the Creature's death, warns against ambition, dies gently smiling, and Walton hears a hoarse voice from the death cabin at midnight.

scenes.title: The Monster's Farewell
scenes.summary: Walton finds the gigantic Creature mourning over Frankenstein, hears his remorse, eloquent self-condemnation, and vow to burn himself on a northern funeral pile, then watches him spring to the ice and vanish in darkness.

Dominant changes from suspenso (~0.48) to tristeza (~0.66) with suspenso dropping, and 224 sustains it with unhappiness deeply impressed and mournful greeting, not a brief mixed blend.

Dominant mood changes strongly from suspenso (~0.48 mixed with misterio/tristeza) in 620-621 questioning 'Do you not love another?' to overwhelming sustained tristeza (~0.86) in 622-623 of weeping self-sacrifice, justifying two tracks.

Left is pure solemn grief at graves; para 683 explicitly states grief gave way to rage/despair with oath of mortal conflict and revenge, continuing into fury in 684. Dominant changes strongly from tristeza to combate/suspenso and stays.

Dominant emotion shifts from strong suspenso (0.65 survival on ice) to tristeza (0.51 vengeful despair plea in 704) with suspenso dropping to 0.33, marking a sustained change from physical danger narration to mournful vengeance oath, not a momentary blend.

Dominant shifts from asombro (~0.45, surprise/admiration at monster's existence) to sustained overwhelming tristeza (~0.96, misery, hopelessness, death) in 710-711, a strong lasting change not a mixed blend.

rejected.reason: No split: left dominant suspenso (0.37) drops, but right has no strong single dominant - asombro 0.275, tristeza 0.259, misterio 0.243 is a mixed blend. Narrative continues same rescue/discovery moment, astonishment is part of ongoing suspense, not a sustained new mood.

No strong sustained break: both 82 and 83-84 remain positive nostalgic Harmonious Childhood - wonder/curiosity shifting to calm/happy domestic friendship. Right mood is a mixed calma+alegria blend (0.46 vs 0.43), not a strong new dominant that stays distinct, so keep single track.

Paragraphs 87-90 are one continuous childhood recollection of discovering Agrippa/Paracelsus. Asombro 0.49->0.35 remains high while misterio 0.17->0.55 rises, indicating a mixed wonder-mystery blend, not a clean sustained break to a new dominant. No new location, action, or scene; para 89's 'fatal impulse' is foreshadowing within same reflection.
